key_insight: The paper argues that weak geometric representations from encoder-based novel view synthesis are not mainly a data or supervision problem, but an architecture problem. In particular, overly expressive decoders can absorb the reconstruction burden and prevent the encoder from learning strong 3D scene representations.
problem_solved: It addresses why novel view synthesis methods often fail to produce transferable geometric features, despite being trained on tasks that should encourage 3D understanding.
method: Analyze encoder-based novel view synthesis through the lens of geometric representation learning.
Identify spatially expressive decoders as the key factor that reduces useful learning pressure on the encoder.
Reframe architectural design to favor stronger scene encoders for transferable multi-view geometry.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it shows that better representations may come from simplifying the decoder rather than adding more supervision. It provides a design principle for building NVS systems that learn features useful for downstream geometric tasks.
visual_elements: Before/after architecture diagram comparing a powerful decoder vs. a simplified decoder
Encoder-decoder flowchart highlighting where geometric information is learned
Conceptual illustration of 3D scene structure and multi-view synthesis
Bar chart showing representation quality with different decoder designs
paper_title: Less Decoder is More Encoder: Geometric Representation Learning from Novel View Synthesis
paper_authors: Keerthi Kaashyap, Dennis Anthony, Akshay Krishnan, Nhi Ngoc Nguyen, Jeremy Collins
